result.title: Ideas On The Move: Mina Guli
result.description:
‘Water is everything, but for too long we’ve treated it as if it were nothing.’

Water advocate @MinaGuliWater didn’t set out to be an ultra-runner, something she says she’s neither good at nor enjoys. But after seeing South Africa's Orange River at a historic low, she knew she had to act. 

Since then she has run 200 marathons in a year, started the Thirst Foundation and helped build a global movement that has reached people in more than 200 countries and territories. 

She joined us at #AMGFL26 in Dubai to explain why water is an issue we can’t afford to ignore.

result.title: Ideas on the Move: Mathieu Flamini
result.description:
‘As an athlete, you die twice, at the end of your career and at the end of life.’

Former professional footballer Mathieu Flamini spent nearly 20 years living his passion for the game. Afterwards, he reinvented himself, co-founding a company that converts agricultural waste into sustainable ingredients used in everyday products like shampoo and detergents.

Growing up by the sea made him aware of humanity’s impact on the planet, and he wanted to use his next chapter to help address it.

He joined us at #AMGFL26 in #Dubai to share what elite sport teaches about business: performing under pressure, commitment and leadership.

result.title: AI and Inequality: Nobel-Winning Economist Daron Acemoglu on How to Get AI Right
result.description:
How we develop and use AI will either strengthen prosperity or deepen inequality, argues Nobel Prize-winning economist Daron Acemoglu. Today’s choices could even put liberal democracy under greater strain. In a special conversation, he shares insights collected in his latest book, “What Happened to Liberal Democracy? Remaking a Politics of Shared Prosperity”, breaking down:

- The forces weakening community and prosperity - and the growing divide between college-educated and non-college workers
- His concept of “pro-worker AI” (models that expand human capabilities, rather than just replace them) and the potential impact on prosperity and economies
- The institutional choices that will have the biggest impact – and the key economic metric to watch in the years ahead

Subscribe to Radio Davos for more conversations on the biggest forces shaping tech and economies.

result.title: These twin-rotor wind turbines can withstand a super typhoon
result.description:
Wind turbines are a key part of the energy transition, but they remain vulnerable to hurricane-force winds, which can snap their blades and buckle their towers.

Ming Yang Smart Energy Group has designed Ocean X, a lighter, twin-rotor model that has already withstood a once-in-a-generation typhoon.

The turbines turn to face the wind and, when gusts become too strong, shut themselves down to prevent damage, after harvesting maximum power.

The World Economic Forum’s Energy Transition Index benchmarks the progress of 120 countries as they work towards building a cleaner and more resilient future.

result.title: Ideas On The Move: Bhumi Pednekkar
result.description:
‘A movie with the right message can actually have a cultural impact.’

For actor, climate warrior and entrepreneur Bhumi Satish Pednekar, purpose has been part of her story since childhood. She sees her platform as a responsibility – and believes personal ambition and social impact can go hand in hand.

Now, she is exploring how cinema could help shift attitudes towards #climatechange. Her approach: tell a compelling story first, while leaving audiences with an idea that stays with them. 

She joined us at #AMGFL26 in #Dubai to discuss why film can be a powerful force for change.
